authority_note: This sidecar is PROVENANCE ONLY. It is not authority and MUST NOT be cited as the source of any Studio contract. Per [STU-SECTION-002] the Master Spec module is the single source of truth; this file records HOW each clause was derived so a reviewer can check the derivation, and so a later capture can supersede a studio_declared value without ambiguity. A disagreement between this file and the module is a defect in this file.

derivation_legend.parsed: the value, field, enumeration or count is read literally from the named record in the named capture file
derivation_legend.derived: the clause is computed or reasoned from parsed records; the reasoning is stated in the note and is NOT itself in any capture
derivation_legend.studio_declared: no source declares this value; the Master Spec declares it as Studio's own contract and the clause labels it as such
derivation_legend.spec_internal: the source is another Master Spec clause, not a green-room capture
derivation_legend.operator_decision: the source is a recorded operator decision or a shipped work-packet contract, not a capture
derivation_legend.declared_gap: the clause declares an absence: something the captures do not contain and which this module deliberately does not invent

REDEFINITION of a v02.205 anchor, not a new clause. The v02.205 text read 'Studio MUST support InDesign-class interactive-document objects on StudioLayer nodes for interactive PDF, fixed/reflowable EPUB, and HTML output.' The source product is Adobe InDesign; naming the object class after it inside an obligation violates [STU-SECTION-003]. The clause is redefined at its own anchor here so the assembler drops the v02.205 wording: an anchor no staged module redefines is carried forward verbatim, so superseding it from a neighbouring clause would have corrected the record while leaving the string in the shipped document. Force is unchanged - same object class, same four output targets, same role-on-a-layer rule, same second sentence carried almost verbatim.
provenance for the interactive-PDF output target this object class is authored for

Enumerates the object class that [STU-PRO-033], as redefined in this module, obliges. Each of the eight kinds traces to the sibling clause named in its table row, so the enumeration adds no object kind [STU-PRO-033] did not already require and removes none. Two exclusions are deliberate and were checked against the v02.205 text rather than assumed: cross-references, index topics, book files and generated tables of contents are long-document constructs owned by the page-layout domain (14.6) and were never obliged by [STU-PRO-033]; page transitions ([STU-PRO-042]) are a property of a spread rather than an object carried on a layer. Including either would have widened the obligation under cover of a naming fix.
the event model these interactive objects bind to for HTML and EPUB output, per [STU-PRO-136]
